summary: Worth one okc check: DEFER has never been timed, and s4's log shows the DEFER kernel passed all 26 eager self-check cases and 6 two-state replays (B=16/32/64, both grids) before the fault surfaced in the 80K matrix. But the brief's rebase premise is false. On master 5d528bf3, variants 4-7 of the sk kernel are already the PSEUDO instantiations, so 'build DEFER as variant 4' would silently become a pseudo launch. Separately, the 1.02x gate cannot route B=32 even if DEFER recovers that band's entire ticket gap.
justification: Target: full decode_16 is 110.8 us (sk kernel 108.2 us, floor 63.2 us, 1.71x the floor). Full decode_32 is 226.9 us (kernel 222.7 us, floor 126.4 us). The ticket-vs-no-ticket sk-diag gap of ~5.8 us at B=16 and ~2.8 us at B=32 is real, and DIAGNOSIS action 4 asks for exactly this measurement. The prior field is accurate: this is the same DEFER mechanism, which was never measured, plus guards. That is a fault-fix stage of a rewrite, not a retry of a measured loss, and nothing in Do-not-try covers it. Evidence on the fault: the archived log tail (archive/full-decode-sk-s4-deferred-ticket-arrive/7f10d2d820cd49ee.log) shows `_sk_defer_matrix raised ... cuCtxSynchronize`. That is the except branch that runs only after `_sk_defer_validate` returned None. So the DEFER kernel survived all 13x2 eager cases, including B=64 mixed at grid 7/SM, plus the two-state replays. The fault lives in a config only the matrix touched. The two new candidates are B=64 x 80000 (5.12M cache rows; no sk launch at B=64 x 80K had ever run, since sk-diag uses only B=16/32) and the variant-5 CNT `_sk_case(count B=.. x 80000)`. The brief's fixes (drop CNT/SKIPM, drop B=64 from the matrix) may remove the fault by avoidance, without identifying it. Per-launch sync+print is therefore the most valuable item: it guarantees the next fault is named. WEAKEST LINK 1, the rebase: the brief says splitkv_attn_sk_kernel and sk_pick/sk_prepare are 'unchanged' on master. They are not. The template is now <STAGES, TICKET, TWO, PSEUDO, TOK>, and sk_pick maps v4..v7 to PSEUDO kernels under SK_PSEUDO. sk_attn treats `variant >= 4` as pseudo (R = 8B; TORCH_CHECK B <= 32, so B=64 is rejected). sk_smem(v >= 4) returns Lay<4, PS_MAXR, true>::BYTES. `static bool done[8]` has no slot for a variant 8, so the host write would be out of bounds. A literal 'DEFER = variant 4' therefore launches the sliding-verify pseudo kernel on full-decode data, which is itself a candidate for a new illegal address. DEFER must be a new variant id (8), outside `#ifdef SK_PSEUDO` so the fallback non-PSEUDO build still has it. That also means SK_MAX_VARIANT and the pseudo/tok predicates must exclude 8, done[] must grow to 9, and _SK_LABELS must be extended. DEFER also goes as a 6th template parameter after TOK, with static_assert(!(DEFER && (PSEUDO || TWO))). WEAKEST LINK 2, the expected rows versus the gate: 1.02x at B=32 needs >= 4.4 us of a 222.7 us kernel, but the whole ticket gap there is ~2.8 us. So decode_32 'faster' is unreachable by construction, and decode_32 will stay on variant 0. At B=16, 1.02x needs >= 2.2 us of the 5.8 us gap. The s4 reviewer argued that most of that gap is the end-of-kernel serial merge tail, which DEFER keeps and can lengthen when a CTA becomes last arriver for both its head and tail request. Dropping SKIPM (variant 6) removes the only measurement that splits in-loop fence cost from the merge tail. SKIPM was not implicated in the fault: it ran only in sk-diag, after the matrix had already faulted. The likeliest honest outcome is a correct run with PATH CHOSEN = master at both bands and the DEFER-vs-v0 numbers printed. That reaches Milestone 1, and the numbers are the useful read.
confounders: restack-sk-pseudo-cluster-plus-v3-fused-preattn: (a) it put FUSED_PRE skF in kernel_fn ahead of _full_decode_sk (`if splitkv and _fused_gate(cfg): return _full_decode_skf`), behind a runtime 1.02x gate it measured at 0.988x/1.014x. If noise flips decode_32 (or decode_16) to skF on this run, that band never reaches the DEFER route, and the shape row moves for reasons unrelated to DEFER. Read the [skF] PATH CHOSEN lines first. The DEFER gate compares against sk variant 0, not against skF. (b) Its PSEUDO instantiations share splitkv_attn_sk_kernel and occupy variants 4-7, which is the numbering collision above.

restack-sliding-decode-sk-window-on-cluster-master: sliding decode_32 (and the sd route) runs splitkv_attn_sk_kernel PSEUDO TOK=1 (14.0 us row in the board profile). Any change to shared template code that is not constexpr-dead for PSEUDO instantiations moves sliding rows. Check that the regs and local-bytes attrs of variants 4-7 match master.

full-decode1-streamk-s3-two-level-ticket: the B=1 TWO path shares the template, and DEFER sits on the !TWO branch. Full decode_1 (sk kernel ~18.6 us) must stay flat, and any move there means the shared prologue changed.

full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: owns _splitkv_gate, which defines the 1<B<=64 band. It does not confound the kernel-row read, but B 33..64 has no scored shape, so B=64 rows in any matrix are unscored work.
interference: No companion is warranted. This is a kind: rewrite stage judged on the sk kernel's own top_kernels row at full decode_16/32 and on the in-prepare interleaved A/B (DEFER vs variant 0 at 2xSM/SM), which costs no check. A loss cannot reach the headline because the gate falls back to variant 0. A gain is attributable on the kernel row, provided the [skF] gate kept both bands on pre-attn + v2. Neither ab-revert nor ab-tune of a landed hypothesis would disambiguate anything the printed matrix does not already. Zero-check improvements to make inside this run instead: (1) Keep SKIPM as a diag-only variant, numbered after DEFER, in sk-diag at B=16/32. It never faulted and is the only split of fence cost vs merge tail. (2) Per the new LESSONS rule (single-round 1.02x selectors mis-routed), measure two interleaved rounds and route B=16 only when both rounds give >= 1.03x with a printed IQR. At B=32 just print the numbers: no gate value there can route a win that is physically capped at ~1.3%. (3) Since the matrix crash is unexplained, also run one eager variant-0 launch at B=64 x 80000 at the very end, after the matrix, with sync+print. That tells the next stage whether the s4 fault was B=64-at-80K-specific (master code) rather than DEFER.
rules_flags: None blocking. _SK_ROUTE is written in prepare and read by config['batch'] only. The tickets stay the existing self-resetting int32 arrays. Host TORCH_CHECKs on workspace shape are shape-only.

The device guard's 'error word' must live in an existing self-resetting/static int32 buffer (not state-sized, no device pointer into state tensors) and must only be read host-side in prepare, never in kernel_fn. A guard that skips a draw leaves an output row unwritten (torch.empty garbage). That is acceptable only because the self-check catches it, and it must never be 'handled' by any host check in kernel_fn.

An illegal address in prepare still poisons the context, and try/except cannot recover it (LESSONS 2026-10-25). Keep this an okc check, as stated, never a scored submit. Watch the 15-minute run limit: import is already ~222 s across 4 modules, and DEFER (+SKIPM) adds sk instantiations to both the PSEUDO and the fallback builds.
open_questions: Which matrix cell faulted in 7f10d2d8? The 16 KB tail lost it. Was it the B=64 x 80000 band (never run before for any sk variant) or the variant-5 count case? If it was B=64, the s5 matrix drops it and the root cause stays unknown. Does master variant 0 itself survive B=64 x 80K?

Will the builder renumber DEFER to variant 8 and fix sk_attn's `pseudo = variant >= 4` / `tok` / B<=32 check, sk_smem, done[] size and SK_MAX_VARIANT in both the SK_PSEUDO and non-PSEUDO builds? The brief as written says variant 4, which collides with PSEUDO single-level TOK=8.
Did FUSED_PRE skF route either full band on this run? If it did, the DEFER result for that band is unread on the scored path.

With the gate at 1.02x (or 1.03x x2 per LESSONS), B=32 cannot route. Is the stage's real deliverable the printed B=16 DEFER-vs-v0 delta plus the SKIPM gap split, and should the expected decode_32 row be 'flat'?
